primary_diagnosis: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Suspected Ulcerative Colitis) vs Chronic Infectious Colitis
secondary_diagnoses: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD, incidental on USG)
clinical_reasoning: A 2-year history of episodic bloody diarrhea lasting 2-3 weeks at a time with lower abdominal cramping, borborygmi, and tenesmus is a red-flag presentation strongly suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease (such as Ulcerative Colitis) or relapsing infectious colitis (e.g., amebiasis or post-dysenteric colitis). Colonoscopy with histopathology is mandatory to evaluate the extent of mucosal ulceration.
recommended_tests: Full Colonoscopy with Ileo-Colonic Mucosal Biopsies
Stool Routine, Occult Blood, Microscopy & Stool Culture
Complete Blood Count (CBC), ESR, and C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
